hypotheses.claim: The bug is that ConstTag client transform always emits a sync $.derived thunk; when the const initializer contains await inside a boundary this yields `await` inside a non-async arrow, causing a SyntaxError at module parse time.
evidence_refs: compiled_client: const number = $.derived(() => await Promise.resolve(5)); inside sync boundary callback
baseline_excerpt: rollup parse error 'await isn't allowed in non-async function'
hypotheses.prediction: Compiling the const tag's initializer with an async thunk + $.async_derived/$.async-style handling (or hoisting the await out) will make the repro compile and render '5' after ticks.
hypotheses.falsifier: If the error persists because the surrounding boundary callback or pending snippet remains non-async and still contains a raw await token, this transform alone is insufficient.

hypotheses.claim: The boundary/SvelteBoundary visitor duplicates const tags verbatim into the pending/failed snippets and the boundary body; the correct fix is to wrap await-containing const initialization in the existing $.async(node, [async thunk], callback) mechanism used by HtmlTag/IfBlock so no raw await remains in sync functions.
evidence_refs: packages/svelte/src/compiler/phases/3-transform/client/visitors/SvelteBoundary.js:44-56 const tags copied into snippets and block.body.unshift
hypotheses.prediction: Emitting `$.async(node, [b.thunk(init, true)], arrow assigning the const)` style output (or awaiting inside an async boundary body) removes the SyntaxError and the test renders '5'.
hypotheses.falsifier: If `$.async` requires the containing block's remaining statements to run inside its callback (they currently don't), later statements reading `number` would run before resolution and the test would fail at the value assertion rather than compile.
